      Case study / Wallet App

      Wallet AppA private wallet that feels native on iPhone®

      Year
      2026
      Role
      Developer
      Built with
      Next.js 16, React 19, Redis
      Code
      GitHub: balances

      OverviewA small password-protected wallet for tracking balances on bank cards and savings jars. I developed it in 2026 with Next.js and Redis, and it can be installed to a phone's home screen.

      9:41●●● ▮

      Live demo with example data. Swipe, tap and scroll inside the phone. Changes stay in this browser.

      Design

      Built to feel like an iPhone app, not a website

      The design is inspired by Apple's iOS, especially the Wallet app, home-screen folders and the frosted "liquid glass" look of recent iOS versions.

      • Frosted glass everywhereButtons, folders, sheets and widgets use layered background blur and colour saturation, so the colours behind them glow through the way they do on iOS.
      • iOS typographyText uses Apple's system font (San Francisco) on Apple devices, falling back to similar fonts elsewhere.
      • Bottom sheetsAdding an account, moving money or viewing details happens in a sheet that slides up from the bottom, like iOS share sheets and Apple Pay. Swipe it down to close.
      • Spring animationsTaps make cards and widgets squish and bounce back with a slight overshoot, like the springy motion iOS uses.
      • Wallet-style cardsBank cards sit in a 3D cover-flow carousel. Tapping a card sends a shine across it, and each card can be frozen or have its full number revealed.
      • Home-screen foldersFrosted folders show their contents peeking out. Tapping one opens it, and the next page grows out of the folder in its own colour.
      • Savings widgetsSavings jars look like iOS home-screen widgets: colour under glass, a small trend line and a ripple from wherever you tap.
      • Privacy tapTap the total to hide or show all amounts, handy when someone is looking over your shoulder. The choice is remembered on that device.
      • Feels native on iPhoneFrom the home screen it opens full-screen with a black status bar and no browser bars, respects the notch and home indicator, and is sized for 390 × 844.
      • Reduced motionIf the phone's Reduce Motion setting is on, animations are toned down.

      Features

      • Several accounts per card, each with its own balance and transaction history: money in, money out and opening balance.
      • Totals for each card and a grand total across every card.
      • Amounts are stored in cents, so balances never pick up rounding errors.
      • Deleting an account takes two taps, so a stray tap can't lose its history.
      • A password locks every page and API call. Signed-in devices stay signed in for 180 days, and changing the password signs every device out.

      Screens

      RouteScreenFile
      /Wallet folders, the home screenfrosted-folders.html
      /cardsBank cards with accounts, balances and transaction historytrading-cards.html
      /savingsSavings jarssavings-jars.html

      Each screen is a standalone HTML file shown full-screen by the app's frame component.

      How balances are saved

      • All records are one JSON object kept in Redis under a single key, balances:records, through the Upstash REST API.
      • On Netlify the same records go to Netlify Blobs with strong consistency, so a reload straight after a save shows that save.
      • Running locally, they are written to data/records.json through a temporary file, so a crash mid-write cannot corrupt them.
      • A live server with no storage set up refuses to save instead of pretending to.
      • Each save is checked: it must be a JSON object and no larger than 2 MB.

      Security

      • Every page, image and API call sits behind one password, checked in Next.js middleware before anything loads.
      • The sign-in cookie is an HMAC-SHA-256 signature keyed by the password, so changing the password signs every device out.
      • Passwords are compared in constant time, and a production deploy with no password set refuses to run.

      Install on iPhone

      Open the deployed site in Safari, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. It then opens full-screen like a regular app.

      View the code on GitHub

      A personal project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple. Bank names belong to their respective banks. In this demo the original card artwork is replaced with plain card designs and example numbers.

      Case study / Urban Suits

      Urban SuitsA suit store you can walk around in 3D®

      Type
      UX/UI design, online store
      Year
      2026
      Role
      Interface designer
      Built with
      GSAP, three.js

      OverviewUX and UI design for an online suit store. Instead of a flat product grid, the catalogue wraps around the visitor as a sphere of cards, so browsing feels closer to walking along a tailor's wall of cloth.

      Urban Stitches / prototype

      Live prototype. Drag to turn the sphere, hover a card to see its fabric, click or tap to open it. Use Full screen for the clearest view.

      The flow

      1. Enter the atelierA needle draws a gold thread down the screen while the catalogue loads, then the sphere spins into place.
      2. Browse by draggingThe collection wraps around you as a sphere of cards. Drag to turn it; it carries on with a little inertia and slows to a stop.
      3. Hover for the clothA card lifts towards you and flickers into a close-up of its fabric, so linen, tweed and wax print read differently before you open anything.
      4. Open a pieceClick a card and it flies forward while a frosted panel slides in with the cut, fabric, lead time, price and sizes.
      5. Book a fittingEvery detail panel ends with the same two actions: book a fitting at the atelier or request fabric swatches.

      Interface decisions

      Designed to feel like a fitting room, not a checkout

      • A sphere, not a feedPieces sit on four staggered rows wrapped around the viewer, so the store feels like standing in the middle of a fitting room.
      • Spotlight in the centreCards brighten as they pass the middle of the screen, while a vignette and soft edge blur fake a camera depth of field.
      • Fabric on hoverEach card carries a procedural macro texture of its cloth, revealed with a short glitch so the change feels tactile.
      • One continuous zoomOpening a product moves the same card to the camera instead of loading a new page, and closing it flies it back to its slot.
      • Filters that keep contextAll, Men, Women, Bespoke and Atelier dim the other cards instead of removing them, so the sphere never jumps.
      • A flat grid for scanningA toggle swaps the sphere for a plain grid of the same cards; choosing one there jumps back into 3D with it open.
      • Always one tap to bookA pulsing gold Book Fitting button stays in the corner on every screen and opens the atelier card.
      • Ready for photographyUntil product photos are added, each card draws a stylised suit silhouette for its cut, from agbada to tuxedo.
      • Works on a phoneOn small screens the filters scroll in one row above the view toggle and booking button, and an opened piece shrinks to sit above its details.
      • Calmer with Reduce MotionThe idle spin, button pulse and transitions are switched off when the system asks for less motion.

      Case study / AI Outreach

      AI OutreachSix agents that apply for internships with you®

      Project
      BASHIR-2.0
      Type
      Multi-agent AI system
      Built with
      Python, Ollama, Google APIs
      Code
      GitHub, MIT licence

      OverviewBASHIR-2.0 automates the search for internships and industrial attachments for university students in Kenya. It finds companies on the map, writes to each one personally and keeps track of every reply, while the student stays in control of what is sent.

      The crawler at work: following the links on a page and highlighting what it finds.

      The pipeline

      From a pin on the map to a follow-up email

      01ScoutFinds IT companies near the student using the Google Maps Places API.
      02HunterCrawls each company's website to pull out a contact email.
      03ComposerWrites a personal application email with a local Ollama model.
      04MailerSaves each email as a Gmail draft with the CV attached.
      05TrackerKeeps every company, email and status in sync with Google Sheets.
      06Follow-upWatches for replies and sends a polite follow-up after four days.

      Safe by default

      • Draft first: nothing is sent until the student has reviewed it.
      • A daily send limit, 50 by default.
      • A random 30 to 90 second pause between sends, so it never floods a mail server.
      • Duplicate detection, so no company is emailed twice.
      • Bounce detection, and no more than two follow-ups per company.

      Private AI

      The writing runs on the student's own computer through Ollama, so CVs and personal details never go to a cloud AI service.

      Mistral 7BLlama 3.1Qwen2.5Phi-3 Mini

      Recommended local models

      How it runs

      # run the whole pipeline
python main.py run

# or one step at a time
python main.py scout
python main.py hunt
python main.py compose
python main.py draft
python main.py track
python main.py followup

# check before anything goes out
python main.py status
python main.py review
python main.py run --dry-run

      Case study / Simba

      SimbaA savings group's ledger in their pocket®

      Type
      Offline-first PWA
      Built with
      Vanilla JavaScript, one file
      Size
      About 68 KB
      Code
      GitHub, MIT licence

      OverviewSimba Women replaces the paper ledger of a real Kenyan savings and credit cooperative. I built it after watching my mother spend hours keeping her group's books by hand. Commercial software expects a desktop, a subscription and constant internet. This runs offline on a low-end Android phone.

      Simba Women / demo

      Live demo with example members. Try Close month, Repay, or the agent button in the corner. Printing and backups are off in this demo.

      What it does

      Everything the paper ledger did, without the evenings

      • Loan bookIssue loans and record repayments. Each member shows as Current, At risk or Defaulted, and two missed cycles flags a default automatically.
      • Interest the way the group counts it20% of the balance every 30-day cycle. Unpaid interest carries forward flat onto the next cycle's due and never compounds, exactly as the paper records work.
      • Sengo savingsDeposits and withdrawals per member, each with its own history. A defaulted member can't deposit until they're cleared.
      • Year-end dividendsTwo membership tiers pool the interest they paid in and split it evenly among members who clear their tier's threshold. Defaulters are left out.
      • Close the monthOne button applies interest, rolls arrears forward and flags new defaults.
      • Tell the agentType "Mary repaid 5000" or "Jane deposited 3000" and the books update. Every change can be undone.
      • Reports and backupsA printable cooperative report, a monthly statement saved as PDF, and a one-tap JSON backup that can be restored on a new phone.
      • Installs like an appAdd it to the home screen on Android or iPhone and it opens full-screen with its own icon.

      The interest rule

      # what a member owes this cycle
due = balance × 20% + interest carried from earlier cycles

# a payment first covers interest, then the balance
paid < due   →  shortfall carries forward, balance unchanged
paid ≥ due   →  extra pays down the balance

# two missed cycles
missed = 2   →  defaulted: no deposits, no dividend

      Offline first

      • Every change saves to the phone straight away, so the books survive a refresh, a restart or a dead network.
      • A small service worker serves the app from cache when offline and fetches fresh code when a connection is back.
      • There is no backend. Members' financial data never leaves the phone it was entered on.
      • The whole app is one HTML file of about 68 KB plus icons, smaller than most framework runtimes on their own.

      Built with

      The app

      HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript
      Interface, styles and all the logic in one file, with no build step
      localStorage
      Automatic saving on the device
      Fraunces and Inter
      A serif for headings and figures, a clean sans for everything else

      Progressive web app

      manifest.json
      Name, icons, colours and full-screen mode
      sw.js
      Network-first service worker for offline use
      Static hosting

python3 -m http.server 8000
# then open http://localhost:8000

      Deploy the folder to any static host and open the link on a phone to install it.
